statement.zh-TW: 上個月晴川花坊替一對新人布置婚禮，當時已經認列了 {{money:vars.amount}} 的營業收入，貨款約定下個月再收。這個月新人付清了這筆錢。收到錢時，花坊的營業收入會再增加 {{money:vars.amount}}。
statement.en: Last month Clearwater Florist decorated a wedding for a couple and recognised {{money:vars.amount}} of revenue at the time, with payment agreed for the following month. This month the couple paid in full. When the money arrives, the florist’s revenue rises by another {{money:vars.amount}}.

feedbackTrue.zh-TW: 收到錢確實是好事，但這筆收入上個月完成服務時就認列過了。這次只是應收帳款變成現金，收入不會再算一次。
feedbackTrue.en: Receiving the money is good news, but this revenue was already recognised last month when the service was completed. This time a receivable simply turns into cash; the revenue is not counted again.

feedbackFalse.zh-TW: 答對了。收款只是把應收帳款換成現金，兩個都是資產，損益表完全不動。
feedbackFalse.en: That’s right. Collecting the money swaps a receivable for cash, both of which are assets; the income statement does not move at all.

explanation.zh-TW: 同一筆生意只認列一次收入。賒銷時收入增加、應收帳款增加；收款時應收帳款減少、現金增加。如果收款時再記一次收入，這筆生意就被算了兩次。
explanation.en: One job yields revenue only once. At the credit sale, revenue and receivables rise; at collection, receivables fall and cash rises. Recording revenue again at collection would count the same job twice.
